items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Andy didn't want to lose Mary Lou, so he was stuck with four trumpeters because McGhee had been sent to him by Glaser and he was obliged to keep him.

ctx.x: I was in St. Louis on Sunday the 7th of December, 1941, when an extra edition of newspapers came out with the news that the Japanese had bombarded Pearl Harbour, but I really got the news from Al Sears who came to my room in the Booker Washington Hotel and told me that he was going to have his family leave New York because he though the Japanese may bombard the Apple next.

During the week, Harold Baker, who was Mary Lou's ole man, had a dispute with Mary and gave Andy his notice and said that he was going to stay in St. Louis. I think that he had over accepted to work with some orchestra. So Andy had contacted his booking agency which was Joe Glaser, the one that booked Armstrong also, and asked Joe to send him a trumpet player to replace Harold. Two days before we closed, a trumpet player named Howard McGhee arrived. Andy called a rehearsal for the next afternoon and when I…

Then arrived the day for us to leave St. Louis and Harold "Shorty Boo" Baker had changed his mind and couldn't stand to let his sweet Mary Lou leave him, and it seems as though Mary Lou may have left the band if Andy hadn't agreed to take Shorty back. Andy didn't want to lose Mary Lou, so he was stuck with four trumpeters because McGhee had been sent to him by Glaser and he was obliged to keep him.

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Dad had three brothers: JOHN, the eldest, HOWARD and ERNEST.

ctx.x: I was born in a place called CENTERVILLE, Kentucky, U.S.A., but my passport says that I was born in PARIS, KY, and the reason is that CENTERVILLE IS an BOURBON County and there was no court house, jail, police, or any one that represented the law. So the births were recorded in PARIS which was the ruling center of BOURBON County.

I was named WILLIAM JOHNSON COLEMAN, WILLIAM JOHNSON was the name of my grandfather on my mother's side. My father's name was ROBERT HENRY COLEMAN and most people called him HENRY. My Mother's name was ROBERTA JOHNSON. Dad had three brothers: JOHN, the eldest, HOWARD and ERNEST. Also one sister named AMANDA, but she was married to a Mr. SAM SPARKS when I was old enough to know her. My mother had three brothers. [ISIAH] ISIAH, WILLIS and PETER JOHNSON, and one sister named SARAH who was married to a Mr. CHENAULT.…

I must have been 4 years old when I started to realise certain things. CENTERVILLE was a village with a population of 450 people, one Baptist Church, one Episcopalian Church, one barbor shop for men, a general store that sold clothing, farm ware and was also the post office, and had the only public telephone in the village.
